conflicts.quote: Every figure on scanner/positions/settings/alerts renders through `FigureCell` with an explicit `register`; no call site relies on a default
conflicts.why: Verified at source: `FigureCell` is not a value renderer, it is a card. `FigureCell.tsx:72-106` styles `CellCard` with `overflow: 'hidden'` (`:77`) and a hover `transform: translateY(-2px)` (`:94-101`); `:302-329` renders a label row, a body and a caption row; `:307` mounts `AccessibleHelp`, which the file's own header (`:26-28`) records as a real focusable `button`. Two shipped structures on the scanner refuse that shape. (a) `ScanCard.tsx:54-59` makes the ENTIRE card one anchor — `component={RouterLink} to={`/ticker/${row.symbol}`}` — and `no-overflow.spec.ts:938` pins it (`toHaveAttribute('href', '/ticker/SPY')`); a focusable `button` inside that anchor is interactive content nested in a link, and the scanner already passes help text today (`ScanCells.tsx:115,132-140`), so `info` is not optional there. (b) In the table, cells sit in `<td>`s with `whiteSpace: 'nowrap'` and a `position: sticky` first column (`ScanTable.tsx:62-63`), and the column header already IS the label row (`ScanTable.tsx:107-145`), so a per-cell card duplicates the label eleven times per row and clips the sticky column. U-1 as written cannot be satisfied on `/scanner` without deleting the single-anchor navigation contract and re-writing a pinned e2e.
conflicts.proposal: Split the primitive from the decision. Extract the register / vocabulary / container-step branch that `FigureCell.tsx:250-300` computes into a pure module; `FigureCell` calls it and so do the `ScanCells.tsx` atoms. Scanner cells then carry the same register, the same closed-nine literal branch and the same step declaration with no card chrome, no second label row and no nested button. Reword U-1 to 'renders through the shared register/vocabulary decision' and keep 'renders through `FigureCell`' for the panel-shaped figures (positions header readout, settings, alerts, quiet band). PM's P3 already accepts this outcome-not-mechanism framing; UX's U-1 is the only sentence that pins the component.

conflicts.quote: The price figure carries a live mark only for a symbol whose displayed price came from the stream this session; a symbol still showing the swept price carries no mark **in the same column, at the same moment**
conflicts.why: Row 11 and PM's own row 6 ('The four surfaces consume the one shipped liveness predicate and mint no second one') are mutually unsatisfiable on the scanner, and I verified why. `FigureCell.live` is typed `LiveClaim` (`FigureCell.tsx:171`), a `unique symbol` brand with exactly three mints — `isDeliveringLive`, `andPresent`, `NOT_LIVE` (`liveClaim.ts:26-62`). `isDeliveringLive(live: LiveUpdate | null, streamOffline: boolean)` reads `live.market_session` and `live.live` (`liveClaim.ts:47-52`). The scanner receives neither: the frame is parsed as `{ prices?: Record<string, LivePrice> }` (`useLivePrices.ts:69`) and `LivePrice` is `{ price: number; ts: number }` (`:24-27`). `andPresent` only narrows an existing claim, so from `NOT_LIVE` it can only produce false. Worse, a hand-rolled per-symbol predicate would reproduce the exact defect the canon predicate exists to replace: `useLivePrices.ts:65-70` calls `setOffline(false)` BEFORE it checks for a `prices` key, so a heartbeat frame carrying no prices marks the stream online, and the only other path to offline is a 45s silence watchdog (`:36-37,84-86`) — a dot built on that reads live with the venue closed, which is `liveClaim.ts:41-45`'s stated reason for banning `genuineIsLive`.
conflicts.proposal: The council must pick one and name it, because the row cannot be built as written. (A) No dot on `/scanner` this phase: row 11 becomes 'no price figure carries a live mark'; note UX's U-5 SURVIVES this, because the F4 retained treatment is driven by the unbranded `offline?: { retained: boolean }` prop (`FigureCell.tsx:174,257-268`), not by `LiveClaim` — the scanner can dim, pause-mark and say `offline · last known` with zero new mints. (B) Add a second mint in `liveClaim.ts` for the prices stream: no backend change, `apps/api` stays empty, but it re-opens the `[one-liveness-predicate]` ledger key and PM row 6 must be reworded to permit it. (C) Add `market_session` and a `live` flag to `/api/stream/prices`: re-opens NO_BACKEND_CHANGE and PM row 67.

conflicts.quote: `term-structure`, `off-exchange-blocks` and `setups` carry no `monoFontFamily` anywhere.
conflicts.why: False for `off-exchange-blocks`, read at source: `OffExchangeBlocks.tsx:24` is `const MONO = typographyTokens.monoFontFamily;` and `:79-81` renders `{b.shares.toLocaleString()} sh @ ${b.price.toFixed(2)}` with `sx={{ fontFamily: MONO, fontSize: 12 }}` — real numerals in the mono figure register, from a widget-local font constant. `fresh-positioning` is the same shape (`:15`, `:56-58`) and additionally interpolates the vocabulary literal `'—'` INTO that mono run at `:58`. So the 'four convert, four do not' split leaves two widgets that (a) set a figure typeface from a widget-local constant, which PM row 53 (SB) forbids by name, (b) never step, because 12px is off the 20/17/15 ladder `FigureCell.tsx:216-221` declares, and (c) render a closed-vocabulary member inside a mono string, the inversion ruling 3 exists to prevent. Only `TermStructure.tsx` and `Setups.tsx` are genuinely figure-free.
conflicts.proposal: Split by figure, not by widget: term-structure and setups have no figure and are out of conversion scope; off-exchange-blocks and fresh-positioning have mono runs whose register must be resolved through the extracted register module (conflict 1's mechanism), which preserves their list layout under ruling 6's freeze while removing the local `MONO` constant and lifting `'—'` out of the mono run. State the deliverable as the property PM row 53/54 already writes — no widget-local font constant, no untraced mono figure — not as a count of conversions.

conflicts.quote: Each of the three positions-side members keeps its own distinct tip
conflicts.why: U-15 and U-1 cannot both hold at `PositionRow.tsx:145-153`. The shipped `literal()` wraps the VALUE in `<Tooltip arrow title={tip}>` (`:147-151`) — that tooltip on the value is the only affordance that makes `not recorded` / `unavailable` / `no basis` non-synonymous to a user, and the comment at `:139-144` says it is built once for exactly that reason. `FigureCell` has no value-row help host: `:307` mounts `AccessibleHelp` in the LABEL row with the fixed accessible name `About {label}`, and the literal branch renders a bare `<ValueGlyph>` (`:284-288`) with a caption that is only `caption ?? null` (`:253`). Converting those cells therefore deletes the tips, and U-15's `review` verdict would read green while the distinction went invisible — the failure shape UX's own risk 7 names for negative-space rows.
conflicts.proposal: Either (a) positions table cells keep `literal()` and the non-synonymy assertion is written against the shipped testids and tips (`cell-not-recorded`, `cell-unavailable` at `:164,166`), with positions' `FigureCell` conversion scoped to its panel-shaped figures — the page header readout at `PositionsPage.tsx:181-194`, where UX's U-12/U-13 land anyway; or (b) fund a value-row help host on `FigureCell` explicitly, as a change to the primitive sixteen shipped desk call sites depend on, with its own regression proof. It cannot be left implicit in 'renders through `FigureCell`'.

conflicts.quote: Alert **event messages** are built from the closed lookups, so stored history renders the same labels as the rule list
conflicts.why: The first clause is buildable; the second is not, without a durable shape change both of us excluded. `AlertEvent` (`features/alerts/types.ts:27-37`) persists a pre-rendered `message: string` (`:32`) and carries only `kind` and `symbol` — no `level`, no `scoreMin`. `AlertsPage.tsx:225` renders `{e.message}` verbatim. Fixing `evaluate.ts:73,94,116` repairs only firings written after the fix; every firing already in `convexa.alerts.v1` keeps its string, including `evaluate.ts:83`'s `rule.scoreMin ?? 60` baked into a durable `SPY score ≥ 60` for a rule whose record holds no minimum. Re-labelling history needs new structured fields on `AlertEvent`, which is a shape change on the store the BRIEF calls the sharpest `[loss-free-durable-migration]` risk — and UX's own assumption to me says no shape change on `convexa.alerts.v1`.
conflicts.proposal: Split U-23 into a forward criterion ('a firing recorded after this phase builds its label from the closed lookups') plus an explicit carried-debt line naming pre-phase event strings as legacy content with `types.ts:32` and `evaluate.ts:83` attached. If the council wants history repaired, say so as a decision: it is an additive shape change to `AlertEvent`, read-new-else-old with the old `message` retained as the fallback, never deleted — and then it needs PM row 70's fixture written against a blob authored before the phase.

conflicts.quote: **Settings section navigation** — a persistent section list ≥900 and the same five section names as a horizontal control below it (V6: this is construction, and I am calling it In deliberately, not smuggling it).
conflicts.why: This contradicts my non-goal 12 head-on, and it is a scope call only the owner can settle. All three of us verified the same fact — `SettingsPage.tsx:156` is `<Container maxWidth="sm" sx={{ py: 4, maxWidth: 640 }}>`, a single centred column of stacked panels, so there is no rail. What PM is buying is therefore the phase's only NEW user-facing surface, and it drags obligations no lane has priced: an active-section model that nobody has specified (the canvas draws it as static markup — `design/src/screens/settings.mjs:29` emits `href="#"` with a hard-coded `.on` class, so scroll-spy vs click-only is undefined, which UX's risk 1 also flags as unanswered), a sticky rail (`settings.mjs:6`) with its own focus order, and a second layout below 900 (`settings.mjs:15`). Every other item in this phase is a conversion of shipped code; this one is not, and it is the item most likely to consume the gate.
conflicts.proposal: Owner ruling, not a lane decision. If In: it gets its own per-surface criteria block, the scroll-spy question answered before the build, and PM row 66's 44px clause tested here first. If Out: my non-goal 12 stands, UX's U-17 and U-18 drop with it, and the gap is recorded in carried debt against `design/src/screens/settings.mjs:5-16` so phase 4 inherits it with the citation. Either way, do not carry the BRIEF's 'brought under the same responsive discipline' wording forward — it sizes construction as a media query.

conflicts.quote: Every `Widget` frame ⓘ is a focusable control reachable by tap, Enter/Space and Escape at every breakpoint
conflicts.why: UX is right about the defect and right about the mechanism — `Widget.tsx:245-249` renders `info` as a bare `<InfoOutlinedIcon>` inside a hover `<Tooltip>` with no focusable host, and fixing it at seven call sites would mint the second focusable-help pattern ruling 6 bans. But the single-file fix lands on the frozen surface: `Widget` is `shared/ui/`, and one of the seven live `info=` sites is `StructureHeroPanel.tsx:216` (`info={HERO_INFO}` on the desk's `span={2}` hero). Changing the frame changes the ticker desk's DOM and its a11y tree, which the BRIEF and my non-goal 11 both declare closed ('The ticker desk is not reopened'). This is not a feasibility dispute — it is a scope decision about whether the desk freeze yields to a shared-component fix, and it will surface as desk spec churn if nobody rules on it now.
conflicts.proposal: Owner ruling. If In: state that the desk is reopened for this one shared-frame change only, and require the desk's own shipped specs to be re-run as part of the criterion rather than discovered at GATE Q. If Out: U-32 narrows to the quiet band's five frame sites via a wrapper at the call sites, which I would argue against because it is exactly the duplicate pattern ruling 6 forbids — so my recommendation is In, ruled explicitly, with the desk churn named in advance.

conflicts.quote: **`features/trading/broker/` is untouched.**
conflicts.why: I justified this non-goal by saying the broker view 'is outside the four named surfaces'. That is false, and PM V11 and UX §2.2 are both right against me. `PositionsPage.tsx:28` renders `PortfolioPanel`; `PortfolioPanel.tsx:22` imports `BrokerTabPanel` from `@/features/trading/broker/BrokerTabPanel` and renders it at `:176` as the second tab of the `/positions` route, with the file header at `:8-9` recording that the locked placeholder was replaced by the sanctioned unlock. The Broker tab is a tab of the positions surface, not a separate surface, so PM row 23 ('Every figure in the sim book and in the Broker tab renders with a stated register') and UX U-14 are in scope by the BRIEF's own naming. I withdraw non-goal 7 as written.
conflicts.proposal: Replace it with the narrower non-goal it should have been: no broker DATA work, no `/api/broker/*` change, no change to the `NOT_RECORDED → NOT_PROVIDED` per-surface substitution that `notANumber.ts:15-16` records as deliberate — while accepting the broker tab's figures as in scope for register enforcement and for the non-synonymy assertion, phrased as UX's three checkable facts (sim renders `not recorded` and never `not provided`; broker the reverse; `no basis` only on `pl_pct`) rather than as a count.

conflicts.quote: **PM will not require a per-figure live dot on `/scanner`'s price column.**
conflicts.why: Falsified: PM row 11 and UX U-4 both require exactly that dot. I withdraw the assumption, and I withdraw the consequence I attached to it. I wrote that requiring the mark means 'choosing option C and reopening NO_BACKEND_CHANGE'. That skipped my own option B and is wrong as an exclusive-or: a second mint added inside `liveClaim.ts` needs no backend change at all and keeps PM row 67's `apps/api` diff empty. The real cost of B is different and I stated it correctly elsewhere — it produces a second answer to the liveness question, which is the `[one-liveness-predicate]` ledger key and which PM row 6 forbids in the same criteria set. The honest menu is A / B / C as priced in conflict 2, and the owner picks; my R1 presented it as C or nothing.
conflicts.proposal: Carry conflict 2's three-option menu into R3 with the corrected costs — A costs an under-claim on a demonstrably ticking price (and my R1 risk 5 still stands: it must be written into the criterion as a deliberate state with its cause, or GATE Q bounces it); B costs the ledger key and a reworded PM row 6; C costs the empty-backend-diff feasibility claim. I still recommend A for this phase, but I no longer claim B is unavailable without touching `apps/api`.

conflicts.quote: **The settings rail is not built** as stated in BRIEF (e) — see C2 and Risk 4.
conflicts.why: All three of us verified there is no rail today (`apps/dashboard/src/app/features/auth/SettingsPage.tsx:156` is a 640px centred column of five stacked panels), so the disagreement is not about the fact — it is about the scope call that follows from it. Architect's Risk 4 rests on 'a new user-facing surface, which the working agreement says needs a design canvas *before* the build'; that canvas already exists and is committed: `design/src/screens/settings.mjs:1` ('Settings — section rail + content column; credentials separated from trader inputs. Rail → tabs under 900px'), `:5` (`grid-template-columns: 220px minmax(0, 760px)`), `:28-31` (the rail naming Account · Preferences · Risk inputs · AI providers · Brokerage, the shipped panel headings), `:15` (`@media (max-width: 899px)` turning the rail horizontal). The stated blocker is therefore already cleared. My R1 put this In deliberately (scope In 6, call P2) and UX wrote U-17 against it; dropping it silently is the scope reduction this round exists to prevent. The trader-facing cost of dropping it: on a 1280 desk, reaching Brokerage means scrolling past four unrelated panels including credentials.
conflicts.proposal: Owner ruling, one of two, recorded either way. (a) IN, scoped to navigation over the five existing panels — zero panel-content change, no reordering (`SettingsPage.tsx:226-228` records that a trader input must not be grouped with credentials), click-only (no scroll-spy) unless UX answers otherwise — and sized as new construction rather than as a responsive fix. (b) OUT, with a phase-4 home named in the manifest's carried debt and my rows 37/38 plus UX's U-17/U-18 withdrawn in the same breath. What must not happen is the BRIEF's 'brought under the same responsive discipline' wording surviving into SPEC over a rail nobody agreed to build.

conflicts.quote: **A. Price column renders `NOT_LIVE`; no per-figure dot on `/scanner` this phase.**
conflicts.why: Architect's feasibility fact holds and I accept it: the branded predicate's true arm needs `market_session` and a wire `live` flag the prices frame does not carry (`pages/scanner/useLivePrices.ts:69` parses `{ prices?: Record<string, LivePrice> }` and nothing else). But option A is not merely 'under-claiming'. Two things are knowable today without a backend change: which symbols are stream-fed (`useLivePrices.ts:29-31` — 'Symbol → latest live price. Absent symbol ⇒ no live tick yet; use the swept price') and whether the stream is delivering (`:32-33` `offline`, with a 45s silence watchdog at `:37,84-86`). And the page keeps a page-level prose liveness claim regardless: `pages/scanner/labels.ts:25` reads `Prices live · structure ~3 min · hot names sooner`. Option A therefore ships a page that says prices are live while every price figure on it renders not-live — a page-level claim contradicting its own figures, which is the exact rule-13/rule-18 separation this phase is carrying onto these surfaces. My row 11 and UX's U-4 both require the per-symbol mark. The feasibility half (can one predicate cover a second stream shape) is architect + UX's to settle; whether the trader is told which prices are live is a user-value call and is the owner's.
conflicts.proposal: Owner ruling among three, and reject the fourth. (a) Per-symbol mark on the price figure, gated on `offline === false` AND this symbol having a key in the `prices` map, with its basis line naming the weaker claim explicitly ('venue session not confirmed') so it never masquerades as the desk's branded claim. (b) Architect's option A, but then the `Prices live` prose at `labels.ts:25` is deleted in the same phase so the page and its figures agree. (c) Defer both to the phase that can carry the wire fields, and delete the prose now. What is not acceptable: option A with `Prices live` left standing — that keeps the false claim and removes the true one.

conflicts.quote: **`features/trading/broker/` is untouched.**
conflicts.why: The Broker view is not outside the four named surfaces — it is a tab on the positions surface. Verified: `apps/dashboard/src/app/features/trading/positions/PortfolioPanel.tsx:2` ('the two tabs (Simulated · Broker)'), `:171` (the trader-visible label 'Broker'), `:176` mounts `<BrokerTabPanel …/>` in the same panel as the sim book. Leaving it untouched ships a surface where one tab enforces the register and the tab beside it does not — the inconsistency the phase exists to close, one click away, on the same route. It also undercuts the phase's headline vocabulary criterion: `not provided` is broker-side by design (my R1 V11; UX §2.2's table puts `not provided` at `broker/brokerView.ts` and 'never' on the sim book), so my row 25's middle arm and UX's U-14 would be asserted against a view the phase declines to convert.
conflicts.proposal: Owner ruling: either (a) the Broker tab is IN for register + vocabulary on its figures — still read-only, no new network calls, no entry/order/cancel control (my row 34 stands) — or (b) it is OUT and the non-synonymy criteria are rewritten to assert only what the sim book can produce, with the `not provided` arm future-dated to the `broker-connect` track and named in carried debt. Do not claim three-way non-synonymy as a phase deliverable while excluding the view that produces one of the three.

conflicts.quote: Every figure on scanner/positions/settings/alerts renders through `FigureCell` with an explicit `register`; no call site relies on a default
conflicts.why: Two problems. First, feasibility: `apps/dashboard/src/app/pages/scanner/ScanCard.tsx:53-56` makes the entire card a single block-level anchor (`component={RouterLink}` to `/ticker/{SYMBOL}`), and `FigureCell`'s ⓘ is 'a real focusable `button`' (`apps/dashboard/src/app/pages/ticker/widgets/_kit/FigureCell.tsx:26-28`), so a `FigureCell` inside a scan card nests interactive content inside a link — architect reaches the same conclusion structurally in §2.2, and the card's single-anchor contract is pinned by e2e. Second, and this one is mine: 'renders through `FigureCell`' is not observable without reading code. A stranger at GATE Q can open `/scanner` and check that a figure states its register; they cannot see which component produced it. My rows 1 and 9 state the same requirement as an outcome and survive whichever mechanism architect and UX settle on.
conflicts.proposal: Restate U-1 as the observable outcome and let §2.2's extracted register module be the mechanism: every figure on the four surfaces renders with a visible register (Mono = traced, Sans + dotted rule = asserted-but-untraced), no call site can render a figure without supplying one (proven by a poison run), a not-a-number never renders in the mono register, and the table and card layouts never disagree about one datum. Keep the component name out of the criterion; keep it in the architecture contract where it belongs.

conflicts.quote: **2.3 Positions: the table keeps its atoms, for the same reason plus one more.**
conflicts.why: The tooltip argument is sound for `literal()` (`apps/dashboard/src/app/features/trading/positions/PositionRow.tsx:145-153` — one Tooltip-wrapped renderer, differing by text and testid only, exactly as its own comment at `:139-144` says) and I accept it: those cells keep their tips, which is also UX's U-15. But `literal()` renders the not-a-number members — a different set of cells from the live-derived figures, and it is the live-derived figures that carry this phase's degraded-state defects, all of them in table cells: `PositionRow.tsx:388` renders a bare `'⏸'` as the entire session-delta cell on a stream drop (no value, no vocabulary member); `:378` appends `' ⏸'` as a text character to the Δ-entry cell; `:68` is `const OFFLINE = '⏸ offline'`. If 'the table keeps its atoms' is read as a mechanism, we agree. If it is read as scope, it leaves my rows 27/28/29 and UX's U-10/U-11 with no owner, and the phase ships a positions surface whose header readout is honest while the cells the trader actually reads still render a bare pause glyph.
conflicts.proposal: Split the sentence into two lines so it cannot be read as scope. (1) `literal()` and its per-member tips stay — non-synonymy is not converted away (my row 24, UX U-15). (2) The live-derived table cells still owe the offline contract: a retained value with the last-known clause, or a vocabulary member without it, at reduced emphasis, with the declared stroke pause icon — delivered by whatever mechanism the architect prefers (extracted module, local swap, or the primitive), stated as an outcome so GATE Q can check it on the page.

conflicts.quote: Every figure on the four surfaces and in the eight widgets steps 20 → 17px under 360px of its own panel's width → 15px under 280px, at a fixed viewport width; a closed-vocabulary literal does not step
conflicts.why: I withdraw the universal quantifier over the eight widgets. Verified after reading the other two positions: `apps/dashboard/src/app/pages/ticker/widgets/fresh-positioning/FreshPositioning.tsx:15,56` renders its mono rows at a deliberate `fontSize: 12` inside a recessed list row, so stepping them 20 → 17 → 15 would enlarge them and break ruling 6's layout freeze, which my own scope Out already forbids reopening; `term-structure` and `setups` carry no figures at all to step (architect C3, UX §2.5). Row 7 as written is either unsatisfiable or it forces a re-layout I ruled out. Architect's Risk 2 also lands: a rule-presence assertion would pass while nothing steps ('**No shipped test would catch it.**'), so the verification method in the row was wrong as well as its scope.
conflicts.proposal: Replace row 7 with two rows. (7a) Every figure that renders at the 20px base steps 20 → 17 → 15 against its own **named** `panel` container at a fixed viewport width — verified by a rendered assertion at a narrowed container width, not by the presence of the declaration. (7b) A widget whose figures are deliberately off the base ladder (`fresh-positioning`'s 12px list rows) keeps its shipped size, and every such widget is named with its reason in the build report. Rows 53 and 54 stand unchanged — register enforced, no untraced figure in the mono register — because that is the property this phase actually owes, and it is satisfiable on all eight.

conflicts.quote: The **shipped copy on positions and scanner is not a variable this phase** — labels, tooltips, column names and status wording stay byte-identical.
conflicts.why: I cannot defend this as written, because my own row 29 contradicts it: row 29 requires the positions pause mark to stop being a text character, and `PositionRow.tsx:68` (`const OFFLINE = '⏸ offline'`), `:378` and `:388` are shipped strings. The scanner carries the identical defect class in its status labels — `apps/dashboard/src/app/pages/scanner/labels.ts:205` is `'⚠ Stale'` and `:211` is `'⚠ Error'`, a typographic truth mark standing in for the stroke icon. I cannot forbid UX on the scanner what I demand on positions. UX §2.1 proposes exactly that swap and explicitly keeps the tone and the tips unchanged, which is the part my assumption was actually protecting.
conflicts.proposal: Narrow the freeze to what it was protecting, and say so in scope rather than in an assumption. Frozen: the semantic wording and meaning of every shipped label, tooltip, column name and status on positions and scanner, plus their order. Permitted this phase, each itemized in the build report so GATE Q sees a visible diff it was told to expect: replacing a typographic truth mark (`⚠`, `⏸`) with the declared stroke icon; replacing a raw wire token with its closed-lookup label; adding a new honesty or basis line. Any change beyond those three classes remains an R2-class conflict, not a lane decision.

conflicts.quote: **Therefore: `FigureCell` never enters `/scanner`.**
conflicts.why: I accept the exclusion of the component (see my U-1 self-revision below) but not the scope of the substitute. §2.2 names the extracted module's outputs as register/vocabulary/container-step only ('mono-vs-sans, figure-vs-literal, and the container-step declaration'), and non-goal 4 says 'The register and the vocabulary do.' Rule 13 puts the REST of the state in the cell: the label-row live dot, the pause marker, and the conditional 'offline · last known' clause. Those are computed at `FigureCell.tsx:257-278` from `offline.retained` — none of them is register or vocabulary. If the extraction ships as scoped, the scanner's degraded arm has no host: today `Scanner.tsx:144` swaps one header string, `ScanTableProps` (`ScanTable.tsx:47-60`) and `ScanCardProps` (`ScanCard.tsx:30-35`) take no offline input, and `labels.ts:30-32` already promises 'the figures stay, dimmed, and say why' — a promise nothing renders. My U-5 and pm rows 12/13 would then go green against prose, which is the exact vacuity shape the architect's own Risk 2 names.
conflicts.proposal: Extract the whole F1–F9 branch (`FigureCell.tsx:250-300`), not just the register/vocabulary branch: a pure function returning `{ figureState, mono, isFigure, showDot, showPause, caption }`, with `data-figure-state` emitted by every consumer. `FigureCell` becomes one caller; `ScanCells` atoms and `PositionRow` cells are the others, each keeping its own chrome (no card, no label row, no hover lift). Then U-5 / rows 12-13 / 27-28 are assertable on the DOM marker on every surface, and the atoms keep their shipped tooltips and `aria-describedby`.

conflicts.quote: **C4 — positions already conforms to rule 24; the scanner does not.**
conflicts.why: Half true, and the false half is load-bearing for non-goal 5. `literal()` (`PositionRow.tsx:145-153`) is Sans and correct, but it is not the only absent-value path on the row. `PositionRow.tsx:374` styles the `delta_entry` cell with `...MONO` and `:377` renders `DASH` — `'—'`, member one of the closed nine (`:70`) — inside it whenever `view.pl_dollar == null`. That is a not-a-number member in the mono figure register on POSITIONS, the surface canon rule 24 names by name, and it survives untouched if the table cells are left as they ship. So 'The vocabulary work is scanner-side.' understates the work by one surface, and a criterion set built on C4 would certify positions as conforming while the inversion renders.
conflicts.proposal: Keep `literal()` and its tooltips — I accept §2.3's a11y reason and withdraw nothing there. Add: every absent-value path in `PositionRow.tsx` routes through `literal()`, with no cell-local `DASH` inside a `MONO` sx. Enforce with the same `?raw` scan §2.2 proposes for font families, extended to `features/trading/positions/`, with the mutation proof. This is one cell, not a re-conversion.

conflicts.quote: **A. Price column renders `NOT_LIVE`; no per-figure dot on `/scanner` this phase.**
conflicts.why: Option A is internally honest only if the page's prose goes with it, and the position holds the prose fixed ('The existing two-speed prose basis (`Scanner.tsx:144`) stays as-is'). Verified: `labels.ts:25` ships `Prices live · structure ~3 min · hot names sooner`. Under option A that sentence becomes the ONLY liveness claim on `/scanner` while every price figure renders NOT_LIVE — a page sentence asserting liveness that no datum vouches for. Canon rule 13 puts liveness in the label row precisely to end that, and pm row 5 bans it by name: 'no surface asserts liveness for a figure by page convention, by a header sentence, or by a widget-level flag'. Under-claiming on the figure while over-claiming in the header is not under-claiming; it is moving the unvouched claim somewhere no test looks.
conflicts.proposal: The owner picks one, and the copy moves with it: (a) option A AND the cadence header stops asserting liveness — it states the two cadences and the price basis without the word 'live' (a scanner copy change pm currently freezes, see my next conflict); (b) the architect states whether per-symbol STREAM PROVENANCE ('this displayed price arrived on the stream this session') can be a first-class rule-13 mark that is not a second answer to 'is the venue live?' — if yes, pm row 11 is buildable with no backend change and the header stands; (c) option C, which reopens NO_BACKEND_CHANGE. I am not choosing; I am refusing the combination of option A with an unchanged header.

(`settings.mjs:30`), while the theme/persona preferences live in `convexa.uiprefs.v1` (`features/auth/localPrefs.ts:15`) — importing that sentence would ship the account-persistence claim pm row 39 forbids.

If IN: it is net-new, it gets a design pass before the build (the working agreement's flag-a-new-surface rule), and it needs three answers — active-item behaviour, deep-link landing at <900, focus order — and my U-17/U-18 stand as written. conflicts.quote: Every threshold a rule does carry renders in the traced register with its unit visible beside it
conflicts.why: Unsatisfiable for the commonest rule without inventing a unit — my defining failure mode. `features/alerts/types.ts:20-22` carries exactly two thresholds: `priceThreshold?: number` (dollars, a real unit) and `scoreMin?: number`, the opportunity score, a unitless 0–100 index. There is no unit to render beside a score gate, and rendering one would be the inferred-unit failure the 2026-08-12 canon amendment names ('A bare number with an inferred unit is forbidden') — where the fix was a visible unit CONTROL, not a fabricated suffix. Second, smaller: 'traced register' is a provenance word, and a score gate is the user's own typed input — neither Convexa's computation nor an untraced assertion. The register has two values and this datum is a third thing.
conflicts.proposal: Split row 47 by threshold type: a price threshold renders with its currency prefix; a score gate renders the bare index beside its closed-lookup label `Score gate`, with no unit and no invented suffix (`≥ 72`, never `≥ 72 pts`). And rule the register question rather than assuming it: I read a user-entered threshold as `traced` — it is exactly the record, reproducible from it — but it should be an owner or architect line, not a lane guess, because it sets the precedent for every user-entered number this app renders.

conflicts.quote: Tinting on this surface stays signed-P&L direction only — never by side, never call-vs-put, never by tier
conflicts.why: As written, row 35 CERTIFIES the surface's worst shipped defect, because that tint IS signed-P&L direction. Verified: `PositionsPage.tsx:147-154` reduces only rows where `pl_dollar != null`, so when every open mark fails the sum is `0`; `:189` paints it `netPl >= 0 ? 'success.main' : 'error.main'` — green; `:193` renders `formatNetPl(0)`. 'Net P/L (open) +$0' in green is a total mark failure wearing the costume of a flat book. `:190` then dims the whole readout to `opacity: 0.5` with no pause marker and no basis clause — F4's costume without F4's disclosure. No pm row covers this figure at all: rows 23–35 are row- and cell-scoped, so the largest number on the surface can fabricate a zero and pass the whole set.
conflicts.proposal: Add one positions row and one clause. Row: with no open row marked, Net P/L renders the vocabulary member `unavailable` — never a number, never a direction colour; with some open rows unmarked, the figure carries a coverage caption naming how many of the open rows it covers, so a partial total can never read as complete. Clause on row 35: '…signed-P&L direction only, and only where the value is a computed P&L — never a zero standing in for an unmarked book.' The dim also becomes the F4/F5 arm (pause marker + the conditional last-known clause), not a bare opacity.

conflicts.quote: Scanner status chip labels carry no `⚠` character and the chip renders a stroke warn icon
conflicts.why: I withdraw U-7. I cited 'Canon's Icons row' as requiring this, and it does not. The Icons row enumerates exactly two typographic truth marks — 'the pause mark on an offline figure and the ring on a closed/replay chip' — and `⚠` is neither. Rule 5 requires 'warning + icon always', and `labels.ts:196` records the glyph as the deliberate mechanism for that ('`warning` binds burnt orange AND the label carries a ⚠ glyph — hue never carries it alone'). So the shipped chip is compliant on the canon as written, and my AC asserted a rule the canon does not state — against a surface pm has frozen. The hazard I saw is real (the Icons row's own reasoning, 'Emoji are never icons' plus 'any platform that colour-emoji-renders them must be given the stroke icon instead', applies to U+26A0 exactly as it does to ⏸) but it is an Amendments question, not an acceptance criterion this phase may assert.
conflicts.proposal: Drop U-7 from the criteria set; the scanner status labels stay byte-identical under pm's freeze. File the question instead: 'does the Icons row's colour-emoji clause reach `U+26A0` in a chip label, or is the glyph a deliberate third truth mark?' — an Amendments line for the owner, with `labels.ts:196,205,211` attached. My U-11 (no `⏸` character in positions) is UNAFFECTED and stands: the pause mark IS one of the two the Icons row names, and `PositionRow.tsx:68,378,388` renders it as a character while `FigureCell.tsx:44,154-156` already ships the stroke icon.
